articles.title: Does Toyota's Hydrogen Truck Torpedo Tesla's Truck Tweet?
articles.content: Toyota's surprise announcement came less than a week after Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) CEO Elon Musk announced that Tesla has an electric truck on the way : Musk's tweet led at least one analyst to downgrade shares of heavy-truck maker PACCAR (NASDAQ: PCAR) and diesel-engine giant Cummins (NYSE: CMI) on concerns that Tesla could emerge as a dominant player in the market for zero-emission heavy trucks. But unless Tesla has come up with a dramatic breakthrough, its battery-powered heavy truck is likely to have a couple of drawbacks: The number of battery cells required to move an 80,000-pound vehicle several hundred miles is very large, meaning that the battery pack in Tesla's truck is nearly certain to be bulky, heavy, and expensive; That big battery pack will take a long time to recharge, taking the truck out of service for several hours a day. Toyota doesn't currently build Class 8 heavy trucks, though it does build light and medium commercial trucks under its Hino Trucks brand.

articles.content: Truck maker PACCAR Inc. (NASDAQ: PCAR) reported first quarter results on April 25, and announced that, for yet another quarter, revenue, adjusted earnings, and truck deliveries came in lower than the year before. A closer look at the truck market and how it's affecting PACCAR Truck deliveries were nearly flat on a global basis, at 35,000 in the quarter versus 35,300 one year ago. Truck deliveries fell more than 8% in North America to 17,000, but were up 6% in Europe, as the North American market goes through a cycle of weak demand, while total truck sales in Europe are expected to be stronger this year than 2016.

articles.title: Tesla Semi Launch: Delayed, Crew Missing
articles.content: Tesla's VP of Trucks, Jerome Guillen , is the only Tesla executive on LinkedIn to have any experience building class 8 trucks. A string of top leaders have already left Tesla this year , including: President of sales & services Jon McNeil (now Lyft's COO) Chief Accounting Officer Eric Branderiz (Unclear current position) VP Finance Susan Repo (now MOVE Guides's CFO) Many other key exes have left the organization in 2016 and 2017: CFO Jason Wheeler (Unclear current position) Autopilot Lead Chris Lattner (Now working on AI at Google) Battery Lead Kurt Kelty (Now SVP Ops at Plenty) VP Business Development Diamuid O'Connell (Unclear current position) VP Manufacturing Josh Ensign (Now COO Proterra, electric bus startup) VP Production Greg Reichow (Now partner at Eclipse Ventures) Greg Reichow may be the most missed alumni. Tesla Semi launch: Delayed It's our opinion Tesla will fail to start production of Semi trucks on time, considering: Most of Tesla's leadership team has no experience building trucks; There is a lack of dedicated resources to work on the Semi program, with much of the staff likely prioritizing Model 3 production issues; Tesla continues to lose critical leaders, affecting its ability to execute on Elon Musk's future product strategies; and Tesla will find it increasingly challenging to recruit engineering talent for the truck project as other manufacturers embark on the endeavor.

articles.title: Why Trucking Stocks Look Like Good Values Right Now
articles.content: Image source Getty Images Valuations and cyclicality As you can see in the chart below, the valuations of trucking stocks like Cummins and PACCAR tend to be far more volatile -- and usually lower -- than those of defensive stocks like Johnson & Johnson and Colgate-Palmolive. There are two interesting takeaways from the chart below, specifically regarding the periods at the start of 2013 and 2016, when the share prices of Cummins and PACCAR rose significantly even as truck sales had peaked and trucking stocks' revenue and earnings were continuing to decline. Clearly, the market decided to buy in ahead of a bottoming in truck sales, and continued to buy the stocks even as their valuations rose for an extended period -- due to the combination of rising stock prices and deteriorating earnings.
